purpose: Compute XNYS full closures and early (half-day) closes for 2016-2027 with exchange_calendars 4.13.2 and compare against an independently implemented second source, pandas_market_calendars 5.4.0 (own NYSEExchangeCalendar in pandas_market_calendars.calendars.nyse, not a delegate to exchange_calendars), reporting every disagreement, to extend market-data-reference gap 5's single-session (2013-10-07) exchange_calendars evidence to a full multi-year, cross-library check.
preregistered: If the two independently implemented calendars agree for essentially all of 2016-2027, that supports treating exchange_calendars 4.13.2 as a reliable XNYS session/holiday source; any disagreement is reported exactly, and a disagreement traced to a realized-bound edge effect (exchange_calendars' first_session clipping the requested 2016-01-01 start) rather than a substantive rules disagreement would not by itself overturn the incumbent, but must still be recorded honestly per year and field.

commands.cmd: /home/example/.local/share/codex-ecosystem/tools/pandas-market-calendars-5.4.0/bin/python3 blueprints/gap-resolution-20260922/xnys-multiyear-holiday-check/compute.py > evidence/artifacts/gap-resolution-20260922/market-data-reference/xnys-multiyear-holiday-check.raw.json   # cwd=/home/example/code/nas-wt-gap-storage-market; prefix pre-existing, both packages already pinned at the exact requested versions

result: 12 years (2016-2027) computed by both libraries, fully offline (no network call; both compute holiday/session rules from hard-coded calendar logic). 1 disagreement out of 12 years x 2 fields: for 2016, pandas_market_calendars reports 2016-01-01 (a Friday) as a holiday, exchange_calendars does not. Root cause identified: exchange_calendars' realized first_session is 2016-01-04 (its default/queried bound excludes 2016-01-01), so the compute script's business-day comparison window for the exchange_calendars arm starts at 2016-01-04 and 2016-01-01 is never evaluated as a candidate holiday for that library, while pandas_market_calendars' comparison window starts at the requested 2016-01-01 and correctly flags it as a non-trading business day. This is a calendar realized-bound/boundary artifact of the comparison methodology, not a disagreement about whether XNYS traded on 2016-01-01 (both libraries in fact exclude that date from their session lists; it is only the pre-bound business-day baseline used for the holiday diff that differs). All other 2016-2027 holiday and half-day computations for both libraries agree exactly, including half-day closes.

verdict_impact.explanation: Extends gap 5's single-session exchange_calendars spot-check to 12 years cross-checked against an independently implemented second calendar library, finding only one boundary-methodology artifact and zero substantive rules disagreements. Supports exchange_calendars 4.13.2 as a reliable offline XNYS calendar source. Does not touch extended-hours or trading-halt coverage, which gap 5's text also names as uncovered and which neither library models.

limitations: Extended trading hours and intraday trading halts remain uncovered by both libraries and by this check, as gap 5 itself notes.

The one reported disagreement is a comparison-methodology boundary artifact (exchange_calendars' realized first_session vs. the requested range start), not independently corroborated against a third, non-code source such as the NYSE's published holiday calendar page; a live fetch of nyse.com was not attempted in this check (not required by the assigned check text, which allows either NYSE's page or pandas_market_calendars as the second source; pandas_market_calendars was used).
